verses.text: Then all Israel came together to David at Hebron and said, "Look, we are your own flesh and blood.

In the past, even while Saul was king, you were the one who led Israel out to battle and brought them back. And the LORD your God told you, 'You will be the shepherd of my people Israel. You will be the ruler over my people Israel.'"

So all the leaders of Israel came to King David at Hebron. David made an agreement with them there before the LORD, and they anointed him king over Israel, just as the LORD had promised through Samuel.
David and all Israel marched to Jerusalem, which was also called Jebus. The Jebusites lived there.
The people of Jebus told David, "You will never get in here!" But David captured the fortress of Zion, which became the City of David.
David had said, "Whoever leads the attack on the Jebusites will become the commander of the army." Joab son of Zeruiah went up first, so he became the commander.
David moved into the fortress, so it was called the City of David.
He built up the city around it, from the Millo all the way around, and Joab repaired the rest of the city.
David became more and more powerful, because the LORD of Armies was with him.
These were the leaders of David's mighty warriors. Together with all Israel, they gave strong support to his rule and helped make him king, just as the LORD had promised Israel.
This is the list of David's mighty warriors: Jashobeam, a Hachmonite, was the chief of the Thirty. He once used his spear to kill three hundred men in one battle.
Next was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty warriors.
He was with David at Pasdammim when the Philistines gathered there for battle. There was a field full of barley there, and the Israelite army ran away from the Philistines.
But Eleazar and David stood in the middle of the field and defended it. They killed the Philistines, and the LORD gave them a great victory.
Once, three of the thirty chiefs went down to David at the rock by the cave of Adullam, while the Philistine army was camped in the Valley of Rephaim.
At that time David was in the fortress, and a group of Philistine soldiers was in Bethlehem.
David had a strong longing and said, "If only someone would bring me a drink of water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem!"

So the three warriors broke through the Philistine lines, drew water from the well by the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But David refused to drink it. Instead, he poured it out as an offering to the LORD.

He said, "God forbid that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?" Because they had risked their lives to bring it, David would not drink it. These were the brave deeds of the three mighty warriors.
Abishai, Joab's brother, was the chief of the Three. He once used his spear to kill three hundred men, and he became as famous as the Three.
He was honoured more than the other two of the Three and became their commander, but he was not one of the Three.
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a brave man from Kabzeel who did great deeds. He killed two of Moab's greatest warriors. He also went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion.

He killed an Egyptian who was very tall, about two and a quarter metres. The Egyptian had a spear as thick as a weaver's rod, but Benaiah went against him with only a club. He snatched the spear out of the Egyptian's hand and killed him with it.
These were the brave deeds of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who became as famous as the three mighty warriors.
He was honoured more than the Thirty, but he was not one of the Three. David put him in charge of his bodyguard.
The mighty warriors also included Asahel, Joab's brother; Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem;
Shammoth the Harorite; Helez the Pelonite;
Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa; Abiezer from Anathoth;
Sibbecai the Hushathite; Ilai the Ahohite;
Maharai from Netophah; Heled son of Baanah from Netophah;
Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin; Benaiah from Pirathon;
Hurai from the ravines of Gaash; Abiel the Arbathite;
Azmaveth the Baharumite; Eliahba the Shaalbonite;
the sons of Hashem the Gizonite; Jonathan son of Shagee the Hararite;
Ahiam son of Sacar the Hararite; Eliphal son of Ur;
Hepher the Mecherathite; Ahijah the Pelonite;
Hezro from Carmel; Naarai son of Ezbai;
Joel, Nathan's brother; Mibhar son of Hagri;
Zelek the Ammonite; Naharai from Beeroth, who carried the armour of Joab son of Zeruiah;
Ira the Ithrite; Gareb the Ithrite;
Uriah the Hittite; Zabad son of Ahlai;
Adina son of Shiza from Reuben, a chief of the Reubenites, and the thirty men with him;
Hanan son of Maacah; Joshaphat the Mithnite;
Uzzia from Ashtaroth; Shama and Jeiel, the sons of Hotham from Aroer;
Jediael son of Shimri and his brother Joha the Tizite;
Eliel the Mahavite; Jeribai and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam; Ithmah the Moabite;
Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
